definitions.explanation: A vehicle equipped to tow or haul other vehicles, typically broken-down or illegally parked cars.
A powered vehicle designed to pull trailers, heavy equipment, or other loads. Includes agricultural tractors and the cab units of articulated trucks.

examples.japanese: {故障|こしょう}{車|しゃ}を{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}で{運|はこ}んだ。
examples.english: The broken-down car was transported by a tow truck.

examples.japanese: {違法|いほう}{駐車|ちゅうしゃ}の{車|くるま}が{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}で{撤去|てっきょ}された。
examples.english: The illegally parked car was removed by a tow truck.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}{現場|げんば}に{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}が{到着|とうちゃく}するまで{1時間|いちじかん}かかった。
examples.english: It took an hour for the tow truck to arrive at the accident scene.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}の{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}がトレーラーを{引|ひ}いている。
examples.english: A large tractor is pulling a trailer.

examples.japanese: {農場|のうじょう}では{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}で{重|おも}い{機材|きざい}を{移動|いどう}させる。
examples.english: On the farm, a tractor is used to move heavy equipment.

examples.japanese: この{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}は{最大|さいだい}{20|にじゅう}トンの{荷物|にもつ}を{牽引|けんいん}できる。
examples.english: This tractor can tow loads up to 20 tons.

notes:
A compound of {牽引|けんいん} (towing, pulling) and {車|しゃ} (vehicle). The word covers both roadside-assistance tow trucks and industrial/agricultural towing vehicles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}を{呼|よ}ぶ: to call a tow truck
- {牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}で{運|はこ}ぶ: to transport by tow truck
- {大型|おおがた}{牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}: large towing vehicle
- {牽引|けんいん}{車|しゃ}{免許|めんきょ}: towing vehicle license

SIMILAR WORDS:
- レッカー{車|しゃ}: wrecker, tow truck — specifically the roadside-assistance type; more common in everyday speech
- トラクター: tractor — the loanword used more commonly for agricultural tractors
- {牽引|けんいん}{免許|めんきょ}: towing license — the additional license needed to tow trailers in Japan
